title: Customer Gravity Index: Weighted Intake & Roadmap Windowing for Strategic Accounts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal:
Define and operationalize a repeatable, signal-driven intake & prioritization mechanism for strategic (top-tier) accounts that balances speed-to-commit with confidence. The mechanism — the Customer Gravity Index (CGI) — will combine revenue runway, renewal risk, integration effort, technical dependency, and strategic adjacency into a single weighted score used to place requests into time-boxed roadmap windows and commitment buckets.

Background / Problem:
Currently high-touch account asks arrive via multiple channels (AE, CSM, Sales Engineering, Escalations). Prioritization is subjective, takes engineering cycles, and often forces slow, large-scoped commits or ad-hoc one-off fixes. Sales expects timely commitments; Eng expects clear, measurable acceptance criteria and rollback/fallback policies. We need a deterministic intake that: (1) triages fast (<=72h), (2) quantifies commitment guarantees with confidence signals, (3) maps to roadmap windows (next sprint, next quarter, backlog) and (4) exposes trade-offs to stakeholders.

Success criteria (OKRs / metrics):
- Triage SLA: 95% of top-account intake items categorized within 72 hours.
- Commitment accuracy: For items placed in a 60-day commitment window, >= 80% delivered or transitioned with documented fallback.
- Sales satisfaction (NPS survey for escalations): +15 points vs baseline within 3 months of rollout.
- Engineering throughput: Reduce unplanned top-account ad-hoc work by 30% in quarter following rollout.

In-scope:
- Formal CGI scoring algorithm and weight defaults.
- Intake form updates in Console + CSM / AE intake checklist.
- Commitment buckets and guardrails (Immediate Response: 0-14 days; Near-term Window: 15-60 days; Roadmap Consideration: 61-180 days).
- Fast-fail criteria and automatic fallback playbooks.
- Dashboard: per-account CGI, confidence signals, and accountability owner.

Out-of-scope (for initial rollout):
- Automated code pipelines to enforce delivery (will integrate later with ENG automation).
- SLA-backed financial credits for missed commitments (handled by legal/sales ops).

Stakeholders:
- PM: Maya Chen (owner)
- Eng partner: Liam O'Connor (backend), Priya Rao (runtime)
- Design: Sofia Martinez (intake UX)
- Sales/CS: Rajiv Patel (CSM), Elena Gomez (AE lead)
- GTM leadership: Sarah Brooks

Proposed approach / milestones:
1) Define CGI signals & weight matrix (2 weeks): workshop with Sales/CS/Eng to calibrate weights.
2) Intake UX & form changes (1 week): design + copy.
3) Lightweight scoring service (ENG) + Console dashboard (2 sprints): store scores, show windows and confidence flags.
4) Pilot with 8 strategic accounts for 6 weeks: capture metrics and feedback.
5) Iterate and bake into roadmap intake flow; define runbook for exceptions.

Trade-offs considered:
- Simplicity vs fidelity: starting with 6-8 signals to avoid overfitting; later expand to telemetry-based signals.
- Manual overrides: Allow Sales/CS to override CGI with mandatory rationale and review cadence to avoid gaming the score.
- Commitment windows vs fixed deadlines: Use time-boxed windows (buckets) to maintain flexibility.

Documentation & artifacts:
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Customer+Gravity+Index+PRD (draft)
- Intake prototype (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/AbCdEf/CGI-Intake-Prototype
- Pilot spreadsheet & scoring examples: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xExampleCGIRepo
- Data model proposal (doc): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1DataModelCGI

Notes on governance:
- Every CGI-based commitment requires an accountable "Commit Owner" from Eng and a "Customer Sponsor" from CS/AEs.
- Monthly calibration checks for weights; emergency reweigh triggers on large escalations.
